title: What if Celeste met Mario 64, and they decided they should try skateboarding?
author: ilrein91
selftext:
Misty and the Last Breeze is a fast 3D platformer where you run, wall-run and vine-swing through short stages, then call an air board mid-run to grind vines, ride flumes and kickflip across canyons. It's built in Godot and I'm making it solo.

All the code is written by Opus 5.5, which also helped create the character (from chatgpt image mockups) and animate it in blender. The results really shocked me, I did a one-shot and got an amazing basepoint, which blew up a bit on X and made me want to pursue it further.

The entirety of the levels are just code-driven, which is wild because it makes the total game size tiny. I'm adding some level music with Suno, but Opus did amazing just synthesizing sound effects and the initial tracks with Python.

In order to really nail down level design, I also had Opus create a Three.js gray block scene where I could annotate and provide feedback on things like jumps and platforming before it would pass it off to build it. My main challenge is to make the levels both diverse and exciting while having fun with a lot of platforming mechanics. I ended up including double jumps, triple jumps, backflips, dashes through the air and being able to shoot a bit of gust in front of you connecting with it to get crazy vertical distance and I also added gliding as well. Then of course I had the crazy idea of giving her an airboard which would let her grind rails do tricks and slide down slopes with style.

I've been trickling in inspirations from the classics by adding floating barrels which propel you, platforms which disappear, floating raspberries in difficult spots to get to, swinging off of vines and just in general been having a lot of fun. It's pretty amazing how far I've been able to push this. So far this trailer is the culmination of two weeks of effort. I ended up putting up a Steam page and sharing my incremental progress on X and I'm almost at 60 wish list which makes me imagine a future where I could support my family just building games with AI. I can't imagine a life that would be more fulfilling to live than that.

I've been a lifelong gamer and being able to transform my crazy ideas into actual reality; It's just something that never ceases to amaze me. And this is coming from somebody that's done web development for over a decade!

Happy to share my workflows and strategies for developing this game. So just let me know if you have any questions!

comments.author: ArchitectNebulous
comments.body: What configuration and harness did you use to get Claude to output this? It looks amazing.

replies.author: ilrein91
replies.body: Simply Claude Code -> ChatGPT Concept art for the character -> Blender MCP to build it -> Then a full night ULTRACODE session to lay the foundations. It did super well and caught some fire on X, which inspired me to keep working on it. The rest of the levels and skateboard all were followups, iterated over multiple times to polish.

comments.author: AdministrativeBlock0
comments.body:
It looks nice and I'm glad you're enjoying building it, but there are some major flaws. Just as an example - in several places you have rings with coins in the centre that you entirely ignore and just double-jump over the whole thing (and it looks like you _can't_ the coins or rings in some places). A game level shouldn't have pointless elements like that. It frustrates players.

Mario games do not do that. Celeste doesn't do that.

Vibe-coded games are ace, but you're missing the _game_ bit. This is a tech demo.

replies.author: ilrein91
replies.body: Very perceptive eye. Sometimes you miss coins because the jump wasn't quite right, or you just don't care about getting each one, but I will have an agent track each coin's attainability going forward. Did anything else standout? What other major flaws?
